_about: Leads: candidate ciphertexts found by sweeps and not yet vetted. They are not catalogue entries and are not on the site. Each keeps the id it was given at merge (ids are shared with catalogue.json and never reused). A lead is promoted to catalogue.json by `python docs/_check_catalogue.py --promote <id>` once its "vetting" block passes the gate (README Conventions, "Catalogue vetting bar"; field list in docs/_check_catalogue.py); a lead found read, duplicated, readable with a held key or not a cipher is closed with --close and kept here as a record. Entries 861-1422 were moved here from catalogue.json on 28 Oct 2026: all came from the Oct 2026 archive sweeps, scored from descriptions; the 98 checked on 28 Oct (research/verify_2026-10/) keep that check in status and prior_art.

Salzburger Landeskunde 125 (1985), pp. 395-399; letter held at Salzburger Landesarchiv (SLA), Geh. Arch. XVI/1
seen.extent: One letter of Archbishop Matthaeus Lang, Salzburg, 19 May 1526 (Pfingstsamstag), about 15 lines, ciphered in the passage from 'Wir ... Zwayer vandl' onwards, printed in facsimile-style transcription on p. 397
seen.cipher: Monoalphabetic substitution with Latin-letter/figure/sign symbols, one symbol per letter with a few doubles (e: 2 and 8; f/v, u/w, b/p, i/j/y merged); Ludwig broke it by hand and prints the full 'Salzburger Code von 1526' table and a verbatim plain-text transcription on p. 399 (read also independently by Hofrat Herbert Klein after WWII).

prior_art.decode: Not searched on DECODE's own site (login wall); known.py for Burkhard von Ems / Matthaeus Lang / Salzburger Landesarchiv found only the lead itself and an unrelated 1513-14 Lang item already marked read; not a DECODE-held record as far as the repo dumps show.
prior_art.tomokiyo: No cryptiana page on this letter found by web search (Salzburg 1526 Geheimschrift searches 29 Oct 2026).
prior_art.lasry: No Lasry paper or GL.htm entry on it found by web search.
prior_art.edition: The letter is printed in Ludwig 1985 itself: cipher transcription p. 397 and the deciphered text p. 399; his footnote 4 only says the letter belongs to the context of Vogt's 1883 edition of the Artzt correspondence (ZHVSN 10, p. 168), not that Vogt printed it.
prior_art.literature: Ludwig 1985 (read in full, 5 pp.); the lead's description 'discussed as undeciphered' was a misreading of the web summary, the article opens with the failed computer attempt and then solves the letter.

vetting.key_check: No outside key needed: Ludwig reconstructs the key from the letter itself (frequency analysis plus the 'sch/ch' crib) and publishes it; checked it is a complete a-z table, so nothing further to apply.
vetting.duplicates: known.py searched 'Burkhard von Ems', 'Matthaeus Lang', 'Salzburger Landesarchiv', 'Bauernkrieg': no other record of this letter in leads, catalogue or targets (Ehingen 1525 is a different Swabian file).
vetting.closed: Deciphered and the key and plain text printed by Ludwig, MGSL 125 (1985) pp. 395-399; nothing left to decipher.

leads.title: Prince Rupert to William Legge, letters in code (Dartmouth papers)
leads.correspondents: Prince Rupert to William Legge (also Digby to Legge)
leads.shelfmark: Staffordshire Record Office, D(W)1778/I/i/37-59
leads.folio_note: 12 items: I/i/37, I/i/39, I/i/45, I/i/48, I/i/46, I/i/47, I/i/49, I/i/53, I/i/54, I/i/55, I/i/56, I/i/59. One on linen (53). Two noted 'not deciphered' (56 Digby, 59 Rupert); 49 'in code, without translation'
leads.status: Staffordshire catalogue: 'in code', several not deciphered. Rupert / Charles I ciphers read by Lasry (SP106-3/5 keys) may apply. Not on DECODE (known.py: no hit). Checked 28 Oct 2026: Not opened in detail (Discovery pages did not render in WebFetch). Search found no decipherment; Warburton (1849) prints some Rupert-Legge letters and should be grepped before ordering images. Printed-edition check, 28 Oct 2026: Partly in print. Eliot Warburton, Memoirs of Prince Rupert and the Cavaliers (1849), 3 vols, Rupert-Legge letters 'from the Earl of Dartmouth's MSS': vol. II pp. 406-408 (April 1644, flagged 'In Cipher', Master of the Horse; letters of 18 and 23 Apr 1644); vol. III pp. 27-28 (Oct 1644, flagged '[In cipher]'); pp. 63-64 and 69-70 (March 1645); pp. 73-74 (Hereford, 31 Mar 1645); p. 100 (Daventry, 8 June 1645); pp. 125-128 (Digby to Legge, answering Legge's of 22 June; Legge's reply, pp. 128-131, cites Digby's letter of 30 June 1645); pp. 151-156 (Bristol, 28-29 July 1645). Staffordshire item dates from the TNA Discovery API (28 Oct 2026): /37 = 30 Apr 1644 (Master of the Horse; matches Warburton II 406-408, whose letters are dated 18 and 23 Apr, so date mismatch), /39 = 10 Oct 1644 (Warburton III 27-28), /41 = 8 Mar 1645 (III 63-64, matched on content), /45 = 31 Mar 1645 (III 73-74, exact date), /54 = 8 June 1645 (III p.100, exact), /56 = Digby 30 June 1645 (III 125-128, printed in full as plain text; the 'coded part not deciphered' is therefore deciphered in print). So six of the twelve items are printed in 1849 with plaintext. Warburton leaves Rupert's own name and some name-cipher groups as '[cipher]' or bare numbers (e.g. '92, 352' in the 29 July 1645 letter, III p.156) and says (II p.471 fn) that he gives uninterpreted ciphers only where he cannot read them. Not located in Warburton: /46 /47 /48 /49 /53 /55 (dates not retrieved) and /59 (Rupert, 9 Aug 1645, 'not deciphered'; the last printed Rupert-Legge letter is 29 July 1645). HMC Dartmouth (1887) calendars only Rupert-Legge letters of 1661. Verdict: lead is mostly closed for 37/39/41/45/54/56; items 59 and probably 46-49, 53, 55 remain unprinted, and the printed ones give plaintext cribs for the Rupert-Legge key.
leads.why: Rupert's private letters to the Legge circle in the 1644-45 court quarrels, in his own cipher.

leads.title: Atterbury Plot and Jacobite cipher letters (Plunket numeral cypher; numbered letters 10-19 'in cypher and French')
leads.correspondents: Jacobite agents to Plunket, Layer, Kelly, Compton
leads.folio_note: letters plus key leads: Plunket's numeral cypher no. 3 (35/47/52) and numerical equivalents (35/73/52)
leads.status: Willes / Ashfield decoded much at the time; SP 35/46/47 says one paper cannot be decyphered without more text; SP 35/46/59 'Undecyphered paper'. Keys in the same volumes and BL Add MS 32256. Checked 28 Oct 2026: Dates confirmed: SP 35/45/78 (7 Oct 1723), SP 35/46/59 (c.1723, 'undecyphered'), SP 35/73/52 (Plunket numerals, c.Oct 1722). Not digitised. Keys in same volumes make this tractable. Printed-edition check, 28 Oct 2026: Partly in print. T. B. Howell, A Complete Collection of State Trials, vol. XVI (A.D. 1722-1725), Proceedings against Bishop Atterbury: Report of the Committee of the Lords on Plunkett's cypher and the numerical cypher 1378 = Atterbury ('Illington' / 'Jones'); glosses of cant names (e.g. 'barrels' = army, 'brokers' = lord Marr); decipherers' evidence incl. Mr Willes admitting that one number, 44, could not be deciphered (col. c. 506); the Bishop's defence on Plunkett's cypher (col. c. 560). The trial volume prints the committee's findings, the interpretations of cant names and the decipherers' testimony, but not the SP 35 letters as figure strings with plaintext, nor the numeral cypher tables of SP 35/47/52 or 35/73/52 as tables (glosses only). SP 35/46/59 'undecyphered paper' is not identified in it. Cruickshanks and Erskine-Hill 2004 not accessible online. OCR of the BSB scan is poor. Lead stays open for the figure-string letters; the printed glosses are a partial vocabulary for Plunket's cypher.
leads.why: Jacobite plot ciphers with keys in the same file.

leads.status: ANOM calendar states explicitly 'Lettre chiffrée non décryptée' and 'Lettre et pièces jointes chiffrées non décryptées'. The same volume holds the minister's ciphered minutes (ff. 31, 43) and the Martinique series COL C8 A 78-81 has 20 more 'chiffrée' letters of 1779-82. Not on DECODE. Checked 28 Oct 2026: Viewed 28 Oct 2026 in the FranceArchives IIIF viewer: COL C8 A 77 f. 88 (17 Sep 1778) is a one-page numeric cipher letter, about 150 numbers, clear salutation only, no interlinear decipherment; calendar says 'non décryptée'. Images online. Repo mercier1761 key (C8 A 64) is the obvious first test. Key status 28 Oct 2026 (targets/martinique1778): the sibling mercier1761 key does not fit (28 groups exceed its maximum, output nonsense); the Bouillé code is a larger third code. A contemporary interlinear decipherment sits on C8 A 78 f.123 (11 Oct 1779) and the same code runs through the 1778-79 letters; with it the key has 123 values and 68% of this letter is valued (read in part, a monthly troop return). Not at the read bar.
leads.why: Martinique at the opening of France's war for American independence (1778): Bouillé's own cipher, undeciphered at the time.
leads.verify: Test the mercier1761 nomenclator, then anneal.

leads.title: Filippo Maria Visconti, Duke of Milan → Francesco Sforza, six cipher letters on parchment, Nov-Dec 1446
leads.correspondents: Filippo Maria Visconti, Duke of Milan → Count Francesco Sforza (his son-in-law)
leads.folio_note: DECODE R7902 (f. 110, 2 pp.; Mazzatinti: Milan 1 Nov, DECODE 10 Nov), R7903 (f. 112, 7 Nov), R7904 (f. 130, c. 26 Nov), R7907 (f. 136, 29 Nov), R7914 (f. 154, 12 Dec, 2 pp.), R7915 (f. 158, Cusago 31 Dec); one page each, graphic signs + letters + numerals. Mazzatinti marks each 'In cifre: membr.' and lists f. 131 as 'Traduzione della lettera precedente' (a contemporary translation of f. 130). f. 145 (Duke, 1 Dec, in cifre) is not on DECODE.
leads.status: DECODE Non-decrypted (all six; DECODE gives no sender or receiver, identified here from Mazzatinti). Not in the repo: targets/it1583 viewed R7900-R7915 on 23 Oct 2026 and found none in the f. 68/70 alphabet, but did not work them. f. 131 (not a DECODE record) is a contemporary translation of f. 130, and BnF ital. 1584 (1447) has more Duke's cipher letters each followed by a 'Traduzione' (ff. 5/6, 8/9): cribs for the Duke's cipher of these months.
leads.why: The last year of the last Visconti duke: his secret dealings with Sforza during the 1446 Venetian war, months before his death and Sforza's bid for Milan.

leads.title: Filippo Maria Visconti → Francesco Sforza, ducal cipher slips on parchment (the last months of the Visconti duke)
leads.correspondents: Filippo Maria Visconti, Duke of Milan → Francesco Sforza
leads.folio_note: about 14 parchment slips entirely in cipher, c. 10-15 lines each (f. 5 seen: c. 15 lines of letters and signs, no word division); siblings ff. 5/6 and 8/9 (ital. 1584) and 130/131 (ital. 1583) have the decipherment filed on the next leaf
leads.status: Mazzatinti: 'In cifre: membran.' for each; 'Traduzione della lettera precedente' only after ff. 5, 8 (1584) and 130 (1583). Image check: f. 15 is followed by a clear f. 16 of the same date (probably its decipherment, unlisted). ital. 1583 ff. 110, 136 are DECODE R7902, R7907 (Non-decrypted). The ital. 1583 slips (ff. 110, 136, 162; DECODE R7902, R7907) are catalogued separately with the other ital. 1583 Visconti letters (venice_milan_decode row 0); this entry is the ital. 1584 slips.
leads.why: The Visconti chancery archive and its ciphers were destroyed in 1447; these slips, with three filed decipherments, are the route to Filippo Maria's own cipher and the 1447 negotiations that brought Sforza to Milan; anything read before 1449 would also be the oldest reading in the project.
leads.score_note: Scored from Mazzatinti, Inventario dei mss. italiani II (1887) pp. 285-509, during the Oct 2026 venice_milan_print sweep (research/venice_milan_print/, sforza_list.txt)
leads.verify: View each slip on Gallica (canvas = folio + 2 to 4 at the start) and note whether a decipherment follows; rebuild the key from ff. 5/6 and 8/9; read the slips without one.

seen.extent: 16 images, 12 telegrams of 10 Mar - 20 May 1914 to Setembrino de Carvalho: 10 with cipher (about 200 cipher words in all, most sent twice, body and service repeat), one clear (pagfis 1318) and one clear signature sheet (1323). Senders: E. Pamplona (1317, 1327), the Minister of War Vespasiano de Albuquerque (1319-1323, 1329) and his aide 1o Ten. Rego Barros (1324-1326, 1328, 1330-1332). Longest: 18 Mar, three sheets; 20 May, about 40 cipher words mixed with clear.
seen.cipher: Letter cipher in telegraph words; found during vetting to be a Vigenère (standard alphabet) with an 8-letter key restarted at every word, so cipher words keep the plaintext word lengths. The telegram of 14 Mar (pagfis 1319) carries a contemporary pencil decipherment of its whole cipher text ('Pessoa que me parece bem informada diz saber por parente Rabelo que palacio está cuidadosamente minado'); pagfis 1326 has a pencil attempt 'complot ambici...' on its two words. The other telegrams have no decipherment on or with them.

prior_art.lasry: No Lasry paper or GL.htm entry on Brazilian telegrams is known to the repo (known.py on Setembrino, Vespasiano, Pamplona, Rego Barros hits only the lead itself) and none was found by web search.

Setembrino's memoirs and the printed Juazeiro document collections were not seen directly, so a printed clear text of some telegrams cannot be excluded; the pencil decipherment of 14 Mar is the only reading seen.
prior_art.literature: Web searches in Portuguese and English (criptografia exército 1914, telegrama cifrado Ministério da Guerra, Vigenère) found nothing on this traffic; the nearest work is the SciELO article on the Canudos (1896-97) cipher telegrams of the Arquivo Histórico do Exército, a different file.

vetting.key_check: The 1471 crib (CFIIOIZUPDYBSUDX SBHBCUDJ AFTGC = restabelecimento harmonia Pedro, all three glossed in pencil) is a Vigenère with key LBQPOHVJ restarted per word; that October key does NOT read 1470. But the decipherment pencilled on the 14 Mar telegram (pagfis 1319) gives the key MFTDBSJV in minutes, and it reads the telegrams of 14, 18, 19, 24, 29 Mar and 17 Apr directly, e.g. 18 Mar: 'dr marques porto declarou me seguinte foi feito movimento de terras nos baixos do edificio palacio governo ...'; 17 Apr: 'parece conveniente responder juiz Pernambuco dizendo que apesar nao julgar identicos casos citados contudo acatando sua decisao aguarda solucao definitiva supremo tribunal'. The 10 Mar telegram fits LETCARIV with garbles ('... chefe ... deu parte doente ... confiança'), and the 20 May telegram broke ciphertext-only to a 10-letter key in a short hill climb ('amigo sincero parente dever lealdade avisar general ...'; key not yet settled). Since a key on the file reads most of it in minutes, this is a key lookup, not an open cipher.

vetting.closed: Pencil decipherment of the 14 Mar 1914 telegram on the file gives the per-word Vigenère key MFTDBSJV, which reads six more telegrams; see research/latam_vetting/1470_sample.txt

vetting.key_check: The key held in the same fonds reads the telegrams. GARV..1.1.4 f. 44r ('CRIPTOGRAFIA', Bogotá 31 Jan 1931, Sección I) with the rules on f. 43r was transcribed (research/latam_vetting/1526_key_garv114.tsv). With the Lunes alphabet, f. 153 (Minguerra to Rodríguez, 26 Sept 1932) gives 'vapor Santa María ... informo ... despacharon para provincia Loreto un regimiento de infantería de seiscientos hombres y [otro] de artillería de montaña', and f. 149 (No. 141, Puerto Asís 24 Sept 1932) gives 'a la una p.m. zarpará cañonero dirección Caucayá llevando dos oficiales, ciento veintiséis tropa, noventa cajas gasolina, cincuenta galones glice[rina]'. A Sábado telegram (f. 106) gives Manao[s] and Tocantins with some typing slips. GARV..2.2.1 holds a second key, the June 1932 Presidency key (ff. 6v, 8 and 10: a 5-column letter table explained by telegraphist José Rafael Ramírez). The numeric telegram f. 151 was not tested against either key. Translations: none were seen in 2.2.4; the AGN descriptions put 'traducción' with the telegrams of GARV..2.3.1 and 2.4.1, not opened.

leads.shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Oxenstiernska samlingen E 708 (DECODE R4338-R4341)
leads.status: DECODE R4284–R4341, 8 records in four different ciphers, each its own entry since the one-key split of 14 Oct 2026. Viewed 21 Sept 2026. The two Bremen letters of 1631 (R4330–R4331, riksarkivet1628.html) are read and removed from this entry; R4282 was deciphered by George Lasry (decode4282.html). R4306: contributed partial Dutch decipherment by George Lasry, transcribed with CTTS then solved with Opus 5.5 (17 Oct 2026; sweden4306.html, which also records this project's failed attempt of 21 Sept 2026); pencilled 1632? and Amsterdam attribution remain qualified, four code identities open. R4336–R4337 turned out to be Rusdorff's London letters of February 1625 in a homophonic cipher with an alphabetical nomenclator; key recovered from the ciphertext by George Lasry (21 Oct 2026, PR #72; rusdorff1625.html) and removed from this entry. Open: R4284 (Latin 1628, Camerarius docket; riksarkivet4284.html) — attacked with Latin annealing and against two box keys, not broken; R4333–R4335 (Rusdorff → Oxenstierna 1628, another cipher; rusdorff1628.html) and R4338–R4341 (E 708, Swedish, June 1633, not 1646; glossed in part at the time; oxenstierna1633.html) surveyed only. Narrowed to the unread part and restored 2 Nov 2026.
leads.why: One remaining key-box ciphertext that resisted a first attack, and Oxenstierna correspondence of 1628 and 1633 with a key collection that may hold their keys.
leads.score_note: Scored by rule from DECODE metadata (class from key signals, solvability from key, length and language, importance from the correspondents); not yet reviewed by hand.
leads.verify: Fetch the images and the key record(s); test the key on the first lines.
leads.known: Bremen letters of 1631 (R4330-R4331) deciphered in full here, key recovered from the interlinear glosses (riksarkivet1628). R4282 key recovered ciphertext-only by George Lasry (decode4282, PR #33). R4306 deciphered in part by George Lasry with CTTS and Opus 5.5, 17 Oct 2026 (sweden4306, PR #42); four code values open. R4336-R4337 (Rusdorff, London, Feb 1625) key recovered ciphertext-only by George Lasry with CTTS and Claude Opus 5.5, 21 Oct 2026 (rusdorff1625, PR #72); codes 628 and 701 open.
leads.open: The unglossed code numbers; not transcribed or attacked (targets/oxenstierna1633).

leads.title: Kemény collection cipher letters (R4933, R4935)
leads.correspondents: unknown → unknown (Transylvania)
leads.shelfmark: Romanian National Archives, Cluj, Kemény_XIX_1628 1 and 3 (DECODE R4933, R4935)
leads.status: Checked 22 Sept 2026: DECODE R4933-R4942 are N/A with no decryption attached, and no published reading was found; the collection is at the Romanian National Archives in Cluj, not Sibiu. Split by system 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry). Narrowed 23 Oct 2026: R4937, R4940 and R4942 read with the Bethlen family key recovered ciphertext-only, and R4939 broken ciphertext-only in its own key and read (targets/transylvania1645/, transylvania1645.html); they leave the catalogue. Still open: R4936 (decoded with the family key, not read: g/q look-alikes the 1,704-px scan cannot separate), R4938 (three short spans decoded, one word unread), R4941 (a different substitution, targets/r4941/) and the Kemény XIX records R4933-R4935 (targets/kemeny1628/). Narrowed to the unread part and restored 2 Nov 2026.
leads.why: Transylvania under George I Rákóczi, around the peace of Linz (1645).
leads.score_note: Scored by hand from the new-solves sweep of 22 Sept 2026 (catalogue descriptions, Tomokiyo's cryptiana pages, Gallica notices, calendars and recent literature); not yet viewed on the image. Kind: solve candidate (no known key).

leads.title: Düben to Queen Lovisa Ulrika, system B ('Chiffer n:o 2'), 1764
leads.correspondents: C.W. von Düben / N.P. Gyldenstolpe → Queen Lovisa Ulrika (and each other)
leads.shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Kungliga arkiv, Drottning Lovisa Ulrika, Utgångna skrivelser, SE/RA/710003/02/008/b/K 259, images 118-124
leads.folio_note: 223 images online (IIIF A0073297). Image 107: a full page of 3-digit numeric cipher (groups 17-720, dot-separated) facing a French clear page mentioning the Empress, Saldern; several more all-cipher pages around images 60-125 in a sampled contact sheet; images ~216-220 a folder "Chiffernycklar" and three key tables.
leads.status: Catalogue: "Drottning Lovisa Ulrikas hemliga korrespondens. Brev från C.W. von Düben till N.P. Gyldenstolpe och Lovisa Ulrika 1764-1765 ... Chiffernycklar." Not on DECODE (no Lovisa Ulrika record), not in the repo. No decipherment seen on the sampled pages; interlinear decipherment not checked page by page. The 24 Oct Riksarkivet sweep listed K 259 as keys only; the 26 Oct sample (image 107) shows a full page of numeric cipher. 27 Oct 2026, Brice Dudout (email): Frederick II's letter of 3 March 1765 in this group is printed in the Politische Correspondenz, vol. 24, no. 15458 (one letter; Düben's code letters unaffected; targets/duben1764/). Narrowed to the unread part and restored 2 Nov 2026.
leads.why: The queen's private cipher channel during the 1764-66 Hat/Cap crisis and her dealings with Russia and Prussia; the keys sit in the same volume, so it should read quickly.
leads.score_note: Scored from the archive description and a sampled contact sheet of the online scans during the Oct 2026 Riksarkivet sweep (research/scandinavia/)
leads.verify: Page through the 223 images (bildvisning A0073297), list the cipher pages, check for interlinear decipherments, transcribe the key tables at images ~217-220 and test them on image 107.
leads.prior_art: partial: interlinear decipherment of the 15 Nov 1765 letter written on the leaf (images 124R-126, viewed 2 Nov 2026); Frederick II letter of 3 Mar 1765 printed in PC 24 no. 15458 (Dudout)

leads.shelfmark: ANTT, Luís de Miranda Pereira, liv. 1 (PT/TT/LMP/0001)
leads.folio_note: Luís de Miranda Pereira, liv. 1; 592 scans online; 'códice factício contendo cartas assinadas, cartas cifradas e cópias de cartas'
leads.status: Cipher A (scans m0265-m0273, Dutch Republic c. 1657-59, three units) located and its letter key recovered from the ciphertext by WAINUT (PR #124, 27 Oct 2026); about 45 of ~290 lines transcribed and read; code groups open. leads.title: Conrad Biermann's copybook, 1675: letters outside key K55
leads.correspondents: Danish German Chancery (Conrad Biermann) → Danish envoys abroad (Paris, The Hague, Stockholm, Hanover ...)
leads.shelfmark: Rigsarkivet, Tyske Kancelli, Udenrigske Afdeling, Almindelig del, "Conrad Biermanns kopibog over udgående skrivelser til danske ministre i udlandet" 1675 (Daisy heid 2130515, unit S-1418)
leads.folio_note: 255 images online (Arkivalieronline epid 15552891; image ids from 48573952). Image 109 (pp. 104-105): French letter with long runs of a numeric nomenclator (2-3 digit numbers 10-672) mixed with letters and symbols (X, #, pi-like signs), no interlinear decipherment.
leads.status: Daisy (new search): "En stor del af de indførte skrivelser er i chifre." Viewed one opening (image 109): ciphertext copied into the register, clear text around it, no decipherment. Not on DECODE, not in the repo. Key lead: Tyske Kancelli "Chiffer" 1670-1709 (heid 2132747, "a mix of many different cipher keys"), fully scanned (epid 15553654). 27 Oct 2026, Brice Dudout (email): Copenhagen to Just Høeg at The Hague, 2, 5 and 9 January 1675, read: 841 of 849 groups, key = the untitled sheet at image 55 of the TKUA 'Chiffer' volume 1670-1709, checked on letters to Meyercrone in Paris in the same key. The rest of the copybook not reported. Extended 27 Oct 2026 (Europe chiffrée, documents.html#hoeg-1675, #meyercrone-1675): 37 letters read with key K55, 18 to Høeg (2 Jan-5 June 1675) and 19 to Meyercrone (16 Feb-21 June; 6,103 groups, 99.4%). leads.correspondents: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, St Petersburg (I Expédition / First Department; Obolensky, Shishkin as Adjoint) → Russian Consul General, New York (Olarovsky, Lodyzhensky)
leads.language: Russian or French (cover text French; plaintext unknown)
leads.shelfmark: NARA, RG 64 (microfilm M1486, Records of the Russian Consulates in the U.S., 1862-1922), roll 83, target 2 "Cables and Coded Communications, 1893-1910" (original: Russian Consulate New York, box 124); file unit naId 571170362
leads.folio_note: Roll 83 frames 0692-1550 (target 2 starts at frame 0692). Ciphertext circulars in 2-digit bigram-key groups: f.0696-0697 (15 Dec 1906), 0698 (10 Mar 1910, No. 63637), 0712 (18 Jun 1902, No. 281), 0732 (1895, No. 4945), 0742-0743 (No. 416), 0749 (1891, No. 3313), 0751-0752 (13 Aug 1891, No. 3902, c. 330 groups, viewed: clean, no interlinear), 0755-0757 (22 Mar 1895, No. 5078), 0769-0770 (10 Mar 1895, No. 5015), 0774 (31 Dec 1904, No. 1201), 0818-0820 (May/Jul 1897, Nos. 5657, 5700), 0823, 0835-0836, 0842, 0847, 0849; the consulate's replies in cipher f.0733-0735 (No. 519, 1895, Olarovsky); 5-digit secret circular No. 864 "aux Ambassades, Légations, Consulats" f.0703-0705 (c. 350 groups, viewed: clean, groups split by hand into 3-figure parts); 5-digit cables f.0694 (cable No. 63, 22 Oct 1908), 0800-0801, 0880-0882 (Oustinoff); naval-ministry letter cipher f.0805-0807 (5-letter groups with a repeating 2849284928... key line and Russian clear text: decrypted). Key material on the same roll: instructions and worked examples for the bigram keys No. 381 (1893; f.0780-0793) and No. 389 (1900; f.0713-0727, with the 12 Dec 1865 "Pesth" example in plaintext, transposition sheet and cipher), circular on key No. 400 (1905; f.0731), additions to the dictionary key No. 402 (1910; f.0728, 0802-0803), lozungi to recipher key No. 448 "Lambda" (1915; f.0869), rules on keeping keys (f.0759-0764), Naval Ministry cipher No. 383 (f.0863-0865) and Naval key No. 394 instructions plus dictionary (f.0884-0900, 0928-1073), and decode tables (f.1088-1550, "Разборная таблица No. 404" f.1443).
leads.status: Found in the RG 64 bulk_all hits (frames with 2-digit groups in a Russian consulate file); full roll OCR read and two frames viewed (0703, 0751). Some circulars carry the consulate's letter-by-letter decipherment worksheets on the following frames (f.0706-0711 after No. 864; 0758, 0772, 0776, 0794-0796, 0822-0825, 0837), so part of the run was read at the time; others show no worksheet in the OCR of the adjacent frames (1891 No. 3902, 1895 Nos. 4945 and 5078, 1906, 1910). The cipher system is described in full on the roll (bigram table + transposition "transparents" Lit. A/B/D; 3-figure values regrouped in 5s for the telegraph), and keys 381/389 come with plaintext-ciphertext examples. Not on DECODE; known.py: no hit for M1486, Olarovsky, Russian Consulate. Not in catalogue.json or any nara_* folder. || Brackx, issue #167 (28 Oct 2026): M1486 roll 83 (target 2, frames 0692-1550): the system is a bigram-table scheme (stencils A and D; instructions to keys 381 and 389, worked example 0790-0792); only key No. 404's tables are filmed (frames 1440-1446), so the 1888-1905 circulars' keys 356, 375, 381, 389 are not filmed; later circulars were deciphered at the time. Not checked on the film here. Narrowed to the unread part and restored 2 Nov 2026.
leads.why: A run of tsarist Foreign Ministry cipher circulars to a consulate, filed with the consulate's own key instructions and worksheets: rare primary evidence of Russian diplomatic bigram ciphers and naval codes of 1890-1910, and the unread circulars can be tested against keys and worked examples on the same roll.
